en.html:
Warrior and tsurugi: one body. Distance does not cancel the arrangement.

However far apart they may be, the same sights and the same voices can reach them both.

So she too had heard.
The declaration.

The hatred in it.
The intention to kill.

――武者と劒冑は不離一体。

　遠く隔てられていようとも。
　同じ物を見、同じ声を聞くことが可能である。

　故に、彼女も聴いた。
　その宣告を。

村正《…………》
村正《……御堂……》

en.html: According to the popular story, Yamato's two great tsurugi smiths, Muramasa and Masamune, perfected their craft under the very same master. Talent, both had in abundance. Great masterpieces were expected from both. Character, however—that department had gone in completely opposite directions.

Great masterpieces were expected from both. Character, however—that department had gone in completely opposite directions.

ja.html:
俗説に曰く……

　大和に冠たる二人の劒冑鍛冶、村正と正宗は同じ師
のもとで業を窮めた。
　どちらも出色の才を示し、いずれ希代の名物を打ち
上げるだろうと嘱望されたが、性質は全く異なった。
ja.text:
俗説に曰く……

　大和に冠たる二人の劒冑鍛冶、村正と正宗は同じ師
のもとで業を窮めた。
　どちらも出色の才を示し、いずれ希代の名物を打ち
上げるだろうと嘱望されたが、性質は全く異なった。

en.html: Muramasa's character was low and the opinion of Muramasa's own abilities was exceedingly high. Even the master sometimes received the arrogance. A tsurugi was for killing people, bas; all this other business did not enter the calculation. Make it harder. Make it stronger. Then harder again. There was the full philosophy.
en.text: Muramasa's character was low and the opinion of Muramasa's own abilities was exceedingly high. Even the master sometimes received the arrogance. A tsurugi was for killing people, bas; all this other business did not enter the calculation. Make it harder. Make it stronger. Then harder again. There was the full philosophy.

ja.html:
村正は人品卑しく、己の業への驕り深く、師に対し
てさえ時に傲慢な振舞いをした。
　また劒冑は殺人の道具としか考えず、少しでも硬く、
少しでも強くすることにのみ執心した。

en.html: Masamune, meanwhile, had dignity from birth, a gentle nature, and courtesy for everybody. Whoever you were, the manners would not be cancelled on your account. A tsurugi, Masamune believed, embodied righteous martial virtue. Strength must be there, certainly, but beauty must also be there. Merely being very efficient at killing was not the complete qualification.

ja.html:
一方正宗は生来の気品があり、人柄は穏やかで、誰
が相手でも態度は丁重であった。
　また、劒冑とは正しき武の象徴であり、強いのみな
らず美しさをも備えていなくてはならぬと考えていた。

en.html:
One day, the master made both disciples forge a sword. Once the work was done, both were ordered to plant their blades upright in the river.

Muramasa went first. They waited. A fallen leaf came drifting down and touched the edge.

Just touched, mind you. The sword was standing there doing absolutely nothing. The leaf divided soundlessly into two and went downstream in separate pieces.

The other disciples were astonished. Muramasa, proud of that fearful sharpness, leaned so far back that the sword-maker was becoming a bow. The master offered no comment. Masamune was told to try next.

After a little while, another leaf came down the same way. Everybody held their breath. Would this sword also produce a cut of that standard?

But on approaching the blade, the leaf changed direction as if fleeing it and floated past without a scratch. Again they tried. Again the same. Masamune's sword did not cut even one leaf.

Then the master gave the verdict.

—The finest blade cuts, of itself, what ought to be cut, and leaves alone what ought not to be cut. Understand this properly: Muramasa, who cut a mere fallen leaf, does not come anywhere near the feet of Masamune, who cut none.—

So it was to prove. Masamune became revered as the greatest armor under heaven. Muramasa became the accursed Demon Armor, hated and shunned. One received the light of posterity; the other received the darkness.

ja.html:
ある日、師は二人の弟子に刀を打たせた。
　そして、彼らが刀を打ち上げると、それを川へ突き
立てるよう命じた。

　まず、村正が刀を刺した。
　そうして待っていると、やがて落葉が流れてきて、
刃先に触れた。

　あろうことか。
　その刹那、ただ立っているだけの刀に当たった葉は、
音もなく二つに切り裂かれて、下流へと漂っていった。

　見守っていた弟子達は驚嘆し、村正は刀の恐るべき
切れ味を誇って反り返った。
　師は何も言わず、続いて正宗に試させた。

　しばらく待つと、やがて同じように、川面を落葉が
流れてきた。
　人々は、正宗の刀も村正に匹敵する刃味を見せよう
かと、固唾を呑んで見守った。

　しかし、葉は刀に近付くと、まるで逃げるかの如く
向きを変え、傷つかずに漂い去っていった。
　それは幾度繰り返しても同じであった。正宗の刀は
落葉を一枚たりと斬ることがなかった。

　師は告げた。

　――刃とは、斬るべきを自ずと斬り、斬らぬべきは
自ずと斬らぬが最上である。
　只の落葉を斬った村正は、葉を一枚も斬らなかった
正宗の足元にも及ばぬと知るが良い――

　その言の通り。
　正宗は天下一の名甲と尊ばれ、他方村正は呪われし
妖甲と忌み嫌われ、後の世の評価に明暗を分けたので
あった。

en.html:
...A popular story, as I was saying.

Muramasa and Masamune never had the same master. They did not even appear in the same period. The timetable itself is refusing to cooperate.

Guru ek, zamaana alag. One teacher, two different ages. Very accommodating teacher. History says they could not have sat in the same lesson; the story says kindly adjust, the moral is coming. Once the leaf has been cut, apparently the dates also can be cut and arranged as required.

Some connoisseur of a later age made the whole thing up.

Still—it would probably be difficult to say that it contains no fragment of the truth about those two.
en.text:

Guru ek, zamaana alag. One teacher, two different ages. Very accommodating teacher. History says they could not have sat in the same lesson; the story says kindly adjust, the moral is coming. Once the leaf has been cut, apparently the dates also can be cut and arranged as required.

Some connoisseur of a later age made the whole thing up.

Still—it would probably be difficult to say that it contains no fragment of the truth about those two.

ja.html:
…………俗説である。

　村正と正宗が同一の師を戴いた事実はない。
　両者の登場年代には隔たりがある。

　これは後世の数寄者が創作した物語に過ぎない。
　
　だが――村正と正宗、両者の真実の一端を伝えてい
ないとは、おそらく言い得ぬであろう。
